ai.title: Refactor patch apply util
ai.summary: Refactors `applyPatch` in `common/src/util/patch.ts`. Extracts complex hunk matching logic into `getMatchIndex` and introduces `REMOVED_LINE` sentinel for deferred filtering. Search functions now return `undefined` instead of `-1`. Internal refactor only.

eli5.text: You won't notice anything different in your app, nothing changed about how patches are applied for users. Behind the scenes, the code that applies edits to files was reorganized: a big nested matching routine was pulled into a single named helper, the value used to skip already-removed lines is now a clear placeholder instead of -1, and one of the search routines now signals failure by returning nothing rather than -1. The developers added a regression test to make sure previously rearranged edits still apply correctly, so this is purely internal housekeeping.

ai.title: Add regression test for patch function rearrangement
ai.summary: New test case in `patch.test.ts` verifies `applyPatch` correctly handles patches that move code blocks, specifically rearranging the `setupSubscriptions` function within `Client`. Mock data files (`old.ts`, `patch.ts`, `expected.ts`) added to `test/__mock-data__/patch/` to support this scenario. Ensures patch application logic remains robust against structural changes like function reordering.

eli5.text: You, as a developer using the internal patching system, submitted a patch that rearranged the `setupSubscriptions` function inside the `Client` class without any issues, and the system correctly applied that structural change. The new test verifies that `applyPatch` reliably handles patches that move code blocks around, rather than just inserting or deleting content in place. No visible behavior changed for end users today; this is behind-the-scenes work to keep the tool reliable when refactoring internal code.

ai.title: Skip LLM patch generation for complete sketches
ai.summary: Added `isSketchCompletePrompt` to `backend/src/generate-patch.ts`. If the sketch contains no placeholder comments, `createPatch` from `diff` generates the patch directly, bypassing `generatePatchPrompt`. This reduces latency and cost for fully specified edits. Falls back to LLM generation if placeholders are detected.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to make code edits where every detail is already fully spelled out (no placeholder comments left to fill in), it now skips a slow intermediate step and applies the changes directly. You won't notice this while editing, but code generation finishes faster and costs less for those complete edits. If the edit still contains placeholders like "//... rest of the function...", the system falls back to the normal generation process.

ai.title: Fix applyPatch hunk boundary logic
ai.summary: Corrected `applyPatch` in `common/src/util/patch.ts` to properly calculate `nextHunkIndex` by deriving distance from `findIndex` and handling the `-1` return value. Previous logic incorrectly sliced patch lines when the next hunk was absent or at the end, causing context line skipping errors. Added comprehensive test mocks in `test/__mock-data__/graph/patch.ts` and `test/__mock-data__/tmp-graph.ts` to validate patch application on complex D3 graph updates.

eli5.text: When the system applies a set of edits (a patch) to a file, it previously miscalculated where one group of edits ended and the next began, which could cause it to skip over lines that should have been kept or changed. This fix corrects that calculation so patches are applied accurately, and the developers added realistic test data (a sample D3 graph patch and its expected result) to verify it works on complex updates. The fix is live today in the core editing utility, improving reliability for anyone generating or applying structured code changes.

ai.title: Implement prompt caching for file context and tools
ai.summary: Added `warmCacheForRequestRelevantFiles` to pre-warm the Anthropic prompt cache using a minimal 'hi' message with `maxTokens: 1`. Updated `getSearchSystemPrompt` to split the system prompt into two distinct blocks, both marked with `cache_control: { type: 'ephemeral' }`, and applied similar caching controls to `tool_use` and `tool_result` message schemas in `common/src/actions.ts`. Refactored `mainPrompt` to always execute file context updates first, removing the conditional check for empty file contexts. This change reduces latency and cost by leveraging prompt caching for stable system prompts and file trees across multiple turns.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to look at your project files, it now remembers the file list it already fetched instead of re-reading every file on each new message, so follow-up questions about your codebase respond faster. The assistant pre-loads the system instructions and tool definitions once and reuses them across turns, cutting down both the wait time and the compute cost per request. This optimization is live today for the file-context workflow in the core backend.

ai.title: Add checkNewFilesNecessary gate to requestRelevantFiles
ai.summary: New `checkNewFilesNecessary` function in `backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts` gates file retrieval via LLM YES/NO check. Skips `generateFileRequests` when current files suffice. Refactors `requestRelevantFiles` to run both checks concurrently, returning `previousFiles` early if unnecessary. Uses `models.sonnet` for the gating prompt.

eli5.text: Before fetching new files for your project, the system now asks an AI assistant a single yes-or-no question: are the already-selected files enough to handle what you just asked? If the answer is no, it pulls in additional files as before; if yes, it skips that step and keeps the current set. You would notice this only indirectly, fewer behind-the-scenes AI calls happening before your request is processed, which can make responses come back a little faster when no extra files are needed. This behavior is live today for the assistant's internal file-selection process.

ai.title: Backend env validation via t3-env, healthz endpoint, deploy script
ai.summary: Backend replaces raw `process.env` access with `@t3-oss/env-core` in `backend/src/env.mjs`, enforcing Zod schemas for API keys and `PORT`. A `/healthz` endpoint is added to `backend/src/index.ts` for readiness checks. Legacy Docker/GCP deployment scripts (`deploy.sh`, `Dockerfile`) are deleted from `backend/`, and `.gitignore` now excludes all `.env.*` files except `.env.example`.

eli5.text: The backend system now checks its own settings more carefully when starting up, throwing a clear error if any required secret (like an API key or database address) is missing or malformed, instead of failing silently later. When the backend is running, an automated monitoring tool can now ping a simple "/healthz" endpoint to confirm the service is ready and alive. The team also removed the old, manual scripts and files used for building and deploying the backend server, suggesting those steps are now handled in a more standardized or automated way.

ai.title: clean-package.js switches NODEENV to ENVIRONMENT
ai.summary: npm-app/clean-package.js injects process.env.ENVIRONMENT = 'production' into dist/index.js instead of process.env.NODE_ENV. This change aligns the build-time environment variable with the application's specific configuration expectations, avoiding potential conflicts with standard Node.js environment handling. The script continues to insert the assignment after the shebang line if it is not already present. Log messages updated to reflect ENVIRONMENT setting status.

eli5.text: When the build process creates the production-ready version of the app, it now uses a custom setting called ENVIRONMENT instead of the standard NODE_ENV to mark it as production. This only affects the internal build tooling that prepares the app for release. If you inspected the packaged output, you'd see the line setting ENVIRONMENT = 'production' near the top of the main file instead of NODE_ENV. The change is live today for any builds produced from the updated build scripts.

ai.title: Warm search cache after file addition
ai.summary: Backend now warms search cache immediately after adding files in `main-prompt.ts`, moving logic from post-response to mid-process. `updateFileContext` returns `null` instead of empty string for no relevant files, triggering conditional cache warm-up. `system-prompt.ts` splits prompt parts across two text blocks with `cache_control: ephemeral` on second block. `request-files-prompt.ts` adds explicit tool-call prohibition instruction.

eli5.text: When you add files during a chat, the assistant now pre-loads its internal search memory right away instead of waiting until after it sends you the full reply, so follow-up questions can be answered faster without a delay for that setup step. This only applies to the behind-the-scenes system that gathers relevant files for the assistant, and you would notice the change only if you were watching detailed internal logs, where one less post-processing step now appears near the end of a response cycle. The change is live today for the internal team that handles file-context searches.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.63
ai.summary: Version bumped to 1.0.63 in `backend/package.json` and `npm-app/package.json`. Previous version was 1.0.62. No functional changes indicated in diff.

eli5.text: The assistant's version number was updated to 1.0.63, which bundles together a set of recent improvements the team shipped in the days before this release. Most notably, the assistant now remembers what you edited by hand in earlier turns during the same conversation, so your own changes won't get lost and redone. It also understands many more programming languages when reading a project, including Rust, Java, C, C++, Ruby, Go, and PHP, so larger and more varied codebases are described more accurately. The update reached everyone using the assistant today.

ai.title: Add mock data for knowledge file generation tests
ai.summary: Added `test/__mock-data__/knowledge-files/delete-comment.ts` containing a massive `ProjectFileContext` fixture. This mock data simulates a complex project directory structure to validate knowledge file generation logic. Covers internal testing infrastructure for the `common` module.

eli5.text: The team added a large, fake project folder structure to their testing materials so they can check that their knowledge file generation works correctly with complex, realistic data. This is an internal testing tool that helps developers verify their code handles real-world folder layouts, and it is live today for anyone running the project's tests. If you looked at the code repository, you would see a big new test file with a detailed mock of folders and files, but regular users would not notice any change in the app.

ai.title: Add error handling to checkNewFilesNecessary in request-files-prompt
ai.summary: Added a .catch() block to the checkNewFilesNecessary function in backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts to prevent server crashes when the underlying LLM call fails. The error is logged via console.error, and the function defaults to returning 'YES'. This ensures the request processing pipeline continues gracefully if the file necessity check encounters an exception.

eli5.text: If you ask the assistant to create a project and something goes wrong while checking whether new files are needed, the system now catches that mistake instead of stopping. This lets the rest of your request keep going, and you won't notice anything unusual because it quietly assumes new files are needed and moves on.

ai.title: Stricter knowledge file creation criteria
ai.summary: Updated `generate-knowledge-files.ts` and `system-prompt.ts` to raise the bar for creating knowledge files. The generation logic now requires a strong 'yes' on specific context-missing or non-obviousness questions before outputting, and the system prompt explicitly prefers directory-level files while discouraging file-specific ones. This reduces noise by ensuring only high-value, non-obvious project context is captured.

eli5.text: The system that writes internal documentation has been made pickier about what it decides is worth writing down. Instead of recording most changes in a project knowledge file, it now only creates one when a change is genuinely confusing or fills in missing context that a developer wouldn't immediately understand from reading the code alone. You would notice fewer new documentation files being created, and when they are created, they're more likely to explain something non-obvious about the project rather than just restating what the code already makes clear.
